split_policy.primary_axis: tooling/e2e activation behavior before fixture directory label, JSON snapshot, expected report, generated output, drift row, hard-fail row, old-mode label, gate label, retired route label, compatibility label, or migration label
split_policy.positive_rule: activation trigger positives are limited to hand-authored accepted scenario directories whose expected activation contract is owned by the e2e/tooling owner; parser, sema, lowering, IR, and runtime phases get no positive compiler behavior from this fixture family
split_policy.canonical_rejection_rule: drift_* scenarios own deterministic rejection of stale, unsorted, unknown-field, alias-mismatch, metadata-pair-mismatch, line-reference, and missing-required-command inputs; these are not positive acceptance truth
split_policy.strict_error_rule: hard_fail_* scenarios own fail-closed strict errors for invalid JSON, missing/invalid paths, forbidden command text, invalid evidence refs, duplicate rows, dependency mismatch, and malformed source metadata; these are not positive acceptance truth
split_policy.provenance_rule: issues, milestones, catalog, open-blocker, overlay, expectations, expected JSON, expected markdown, expected stderr, and expected exit-code files are fixture provenance unless the e2e/tooling owner claims the scenario boundary
split_policy.retired_surface_rule: old-mode activation, compatibility activation, gate activation, retired route activation, generated-only activation, evidence-log activation, migration-only activation, wrapper-only activation, runner-only success, workflow-label-only success, and generated/report rows promoted as support are canonical rejection, strict-error, absent-support, or provenance-only evidence
